metadata.title: The Three-Dimensional Counterexample to the Jacobian Conjecture: Exact Validation, a Proved Seed-Family Constructor, the Discriminant Wall of Non-Properness, and Planar Equivariant Rigidity
metadata.description:
On 2026-07-20, Levent Alpöge announced (crediting the language model Claude Fable 5) a polynomial map F from C^3 to C^3 with constant Jacobian determinant -2 and a repeated value, refuting the Jacobian conjecture for every N ≥ 3. The fiber over the announced target consists of exactly the three announced points. The map is a weighted skew product over the invariants v = xy, t = x^2 z; its Keller property is a two-variable identity.

We prove a constructor: every admissible seed polynomial p, scale k and section q gives a Keller map of determinant -k p(1)^2 and generic fiber degree deg p + 1. The degree law (5d - 3, 5d - 4, 4) is machine-verified on four seeds; its extension to every seed and the minimality of the announced map within the family are conjectural. The asymptotic variety of F is the discriminant surface 27A^2C^2 - 18ABC + 16A + B^3C - B^2 = 0 alone. F is not surjective, over the complex numbers or the reals: its image omits an explicit curve, and the fibers over C = 0 have three points off B^2 = 16A (computation EXP-145). Version 0.14 stated a surjective real restriction and an asymptotic plane C = 0, both false, and the minimality of the announced map as proved, which is conjectural.

In dimension two, equivariant Keller maps are linear for opposite-sign weights and affine, (f0 x, g0 y + c) or its swap, for one zero weight, so a planar counterexample must be non-equivariant.

Source code, data and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH (problems/algebraic-geometry/jacobian-conjecture).
